creator: music-industry
topic: There is no per-stream rate — the pooled pro-rata structure, not the headline rate, explains why two artists with identical streams get paid differently

orphans: the flow itself as an object — the typed transfer between two parties; every column holds cards about a party, none holds the edge between them
contract terms — recoupable advance, contractual percentage, term; not plumbing, not an entity, not regulation; lands in 'flows' by elimination and corrupts it

the definitional claim — 'there is no per-stream rate' is a category-error claim about the measuring instrument (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:49 names the shape); its only home is 'the-number', where a claim that a number does not exist reads as a number

time_saved.note: Creator's accept bar is 60 min. Residual is dominated by G-L1S-MI-03 — qualifier re-verification cannot be delegated while territory/period/source-class are unstructured. Confidence held low-medium per accepted-gaps.md `scope-note`: the app cannot run research, so this estimates the methodic, not the product.

engine_availability.note: Three of seven render a flow. None is catalogued as a flow engine. F Anchor Ladder is the exact structural match ('one concrete object → progressively harder cases') and is fenced to short form against ENGINES.md:4-6's own claim that engines are duration-independent.

findings.creator: music-industry
findings.topic: one euro from listener to artist through five parties, each taking a differently-defined share
findings.title: `mechanisms[].chain` steps are untyped prose with no fact binding and no per-step parameter
findings.expected: A five-party flow expressed as a chain where each step carries its share, its rule-type (per-stream / pro-rata / contractual % / recoupable advance) and a binding to the fact that establishes it — so a beat can state the share and a descope wounds the mechanism.
findings.got: `chain[]` is an array of free-text sentences. `mechanisms[]` is the only structure in the schema with no `evidence[]`: `reversals[]` has one (:56), `steel_man` has one (:62), `conclusions.restsOn` has card ids (conclusions.ts:44). So the parameter lives inside a sentence with no id, date, source or confidence, is unreachable by the wound graph, and step 4 of the composition procedure — which reads mechanisms for 'beats as one-line claims' — receives a gesture rather than a claim.
findings.refuter_note: Refuted the framing I arrived with: a mechanism is NOT a single link — `chain[]` holds seven steps across three parties in the reference run (notebook.json:216-224), so my flow is one mechanism, not five disconnected ones. The surviving defect is narrower and stronger: the chain is untyped. Tested 'is this my topic being hard?' — no: m-etf-plumbing needed the same binding on a market topic. Tested 'would a competent execution produce it anyway?' — no, there is no field to write it into. Fixable by a shared schema field, therefore `content`, not `lens`.
findings.l2_priority: Write the royalty flow as one mechanism and check whether the rendered script can state any per-step share without inventing it, and whether descoping the fact behind step 3 wounds the mechanism at all.

findings.creator: music-industry
findings.topic: one euro from listener to artist through five parties
findings.title: The BUT/THEREFORE law has no vocabulary for a transfer, and instructs the researcher to delete the flow steps — already silently violated in the reference run
findings.expected: A causal-chain law that can express a quantity moving through parties. Of my five links, two are honest AND-THENs — a deduction is neither a consequence nor a complication — and they are the two parties whose shares are the subject.
findings.got: RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:65-67 says an AND-THEN link means 'find the missing link or drop it', and the quality bar at :124 demands every link be BUT or THEREFORE. There is no missing link in a subtraction, so the instruction resolves to 'drop it', deleting the platform's and the label's steps. Not theoretical: the reference notebook contains two bare `AND` links inside `mechanisms[].chain` (notebook.json:207, :222) under a bar that says zero, uncaught — the vocabulary runs out the moment a chain describes movement rather than causation.
findings.refuter_note: Hardest refutation attempted: 'the law is about BEATS, not about notebook chains, so a flow can be a sequence in the notebook and a BUT/THEREFORE chain in the script.' It fails on the artifact — NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:52 states 'the beat chain is authored here', and the quality bar applies the law to `mechanism.chain` directly. Also tested 'is this my topic being hard?' — refuted by the reference run breaking the same rule on a market topic, which is convergence inside the exemplar itself. Content, not lens: one added connector or one carve-out for transfer links serves crypto plumbing, supply chains and appropriations equally.
findings.l2_priority: Count AND-THEN links in the produced royalty mechanism, and check whether the rendered script drops the platform and label steps or smuggles them in as 'and'.

findings.creator: music-industry
findings.topic: rates that are aggressively policed and never quotable without territory, period and statement
findings.title: `facts[]` has no territory, no reporting period distinct from `as_of`, and no source class
findings.expected: A rate carries three structured qualifiers: territory, the period the rate covers, and the identity/class of the statement it came from — so downstream rules can group, expire and audit by them.
findings.got: `{id, claim, load_bearing, source, confidence, as_of, note?}`. No territory field. `as_of` is defined as the date the fact is true as of and drives `currency` (:47) — a royalty rate has a separate reporting period (a quarter earned, paid two quarters later), and one field cannot hold both. `source` is a free string with no primary/aggregator distinction ('CryptoQuant via aggregators', notebook.json:184). All three are prose-satisfiable inside `claim`, which Rule 1 (:93, 'No prose. Claims are one line') then fights — and prose is unreachable by any downstream rule, column grouping or expiry check.
findings.refuter_note: Genuine partial refutation, recorded rather than hidden: nothing stops a competent researcher writing all three qualifiers into the `claim` string, so the information is reachable. That is why this is `major` and not `blocker`. What survives is that the qualifiers are unstructured — `currency` cannot expire a fact whose territory changed but whose date did not, and the board cannot group by level or region. Also the direct cause of the time-saved bar being missed, which is the impact argument.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether a produced royalty notebook's facts actually carry territory and period in prose, or whether the run silently drops them to keep claims one line.

findings.creator: music-industry
findings.topic: anonymised distributor statements sent by musicians — primary, verifiable by the author, uncitable by the reader
findings.title: `confidence` collapses correctness and reader-checkability; primary-but-uncitable evidence has no honest label
findings.expected: Two independent axes: how sure the researcher is the figure is right, and whether a reader can verify it. My statements are maximal on the first and zero on the second, and both facts must be visible.
findings.got: One scalar `high|medium|low`. `high` launders an uncheckable figure into the register of a public filing; `low` demotes the best available material and triggers :95's flag-for-a-second-source, which here can only be satisfied by deanonymising the musician who supplied it — the audience-protection rule asks the researcher to burn a source. Rule 2 (:94, 'every fact dated and sourced, no exceptions') is satisfied by a free string while the purpose that rule buys — knowledge/README.md:47-48, 'a reader who disagrees can go look' — is defeated, and no field records the defeat. Note also that notebook facts do not use the MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED ladder at all; that ladder governs PATTERNS.md craft claims. If forced onto it, this evidence is MEASURED-but-unreproducible, and MEASURED requires the corpus (:38). No such rung exists.
findings.refuter_note: Real refutation found and downgrades this from confirmed-absent to present-broken: `confidence` carries a reason string in practice (notebook.json:42, 'medium — price sources vary by a few thousand'), so 'high — primary document held by author, not reader-verifiable' is writable today. It is the workaround I would use. It fails because it is free text nothing downstream reads, and the flagging rule at :95 keys off the enum, not the reason. Contradicts the brief's hypothesis 2 as stated: the ladder is not the problem, because the notebook never uses it.
findings.l2_priority: Attempt a notebook using an anonymised primary source as a load-bearing fact and record which confidence value was chosen and what the flagging rule then demanded.

findings.creator: music-industry
findings.topic: platform-level payouts and artist-level receipts are different quantities and must never be compared
findings.title: No `party`/`level` on a fact, and one singular 'The number' column — figures from different levels of a flow become neighbours
findings.expected: A figure carries which party and which level of the flow it describes, and the board can separate a platform's aggregate payout from an artist's statement line. Presenting a platform payout as an artist payout is the most common correction in this field.
findings.got: `facts[]` has no party or level field. `DIMENSIONS[0]` is 'The number', singular, with `purpose` 'What the price actually did, and over what window' — a market column that presumes ONE quantity. My topic has one number per party per step, five of them, mutually incomparable, and the taxonomy files them together. `DEFAULT_DIMENSION = 'the-number'` (:62) makes that the sink for anything unclassified.
findings.refuter_note: Explicitly NOT G-000, which is about untagged follow-up cards hitting the fallback. Mine is that even correctly tagged facts at different levels share one column with no marker. Tested 'is this the topic being hard?' — no: any topic with two parties at different scales hits it (platform revenue vs artist receipt, group revenue vs segment revenue, federal appropriation vs disbursement). Content: a `level`/`party` field plus a pluralised column serves everyone.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether a produced notebook places a platform-aggregate fact and an artist-receipt fact in the same column, and whether the rendered script compares them in a sentence.

findings.creator: music-industry
findings.topic: the counter-case has two independent holders — the platform's arithmetic defence and the label's cost-of-capital defence
findings.title: `steel_man` is a single object; a counter-case with two independent holders cannot be structured
findings.expected: Two steel-men, separately evidenced and separately weighable — 'the pool is arithmetic, not policy' (platform) and 'the advance is recoupable because we bore the risk' (label). One can fall while the other stands, and that asymmetry is the most interesting adjudication in the topic.
findings.got: `steel_man` is one object `{claim, evidence[], statement, why_include}` (:61-65). Two arguments must be merged into one `statement`, which makes separate weighing impossible, or one must be dropped. `counter_positions_to_state_fairly[]` (:73) is an array but of bare strings — no ids, no `evidence[]`, no route onto the board; in the reference, the counter-case column holds one steel-man card plus two facts.
findings.refuter_note: Refutation tried and partly lands: `counter_positions_to_state_fairly[]` exists precisely to hold additional opposing views, so this is present-broken rather than confirmed-absent. It does not discharge the finding — those entries carry no evidence and cannot be weighed, and Engine D's honesty test (ENGINES.md:91-93) requires candidates that can actually win, which needs evidence attached. Also contradicts brief hypothesis 4 for this topic: my counter-case is over-reachable, not unreachable.
findings.l2_priority: Run Engine D on the royalty topic and check whether both counter-case holders appear as separately weighed candidates or collapse into one.

findings.creator: music-industry
findings.topic: a flow-following video — follow one euro down five deductions
findings.title: No engine is catalogued for a flow shape, and F Anchor Ladder — the structural match — is fenced to short form against ENGINES.md's own duration claim
findings.expected: The Choosing table offers a row for 'a quantity moving through parties', and the engine whose shape is 'one concrete object demonstrating progressively harder cases' is available at essay length.
findings.got: The Choosing table (:162-171) has no flow row. F is tagged '*(short form)*' at :132 and witnessed only at 57s, while :4-6 states an engine 'does not belong to a duration — a Reversal Chain is a Reversal Chain at 30 seconds and at 18 minutes'. The catalogue contradicts its own opening claim, and the engine it fences is the one shaped like my topic. Engine B's pleasure ('the disproportion between labour and reward', :44-47) also renders a flow perfectly and is described only as a demonstration engine.
findings.refuter_note: Strong refutation, which is why this is minor: ENGINES.md:173-175 explicitly says engines compose and the list is 'a vocabulary, not a menu', so A-with-a-B-spine is available to a careful reader. Three engines would render the topic — not zero, and not seven, so the notebook has real shape. What survives is a discoverability defect plus a genuine internal contradiction between :4-6 and the short-form tags on F and G. Cheapest fix in the whole set: one table row and one sentence.
findings.l2_priority: Record which engine `engine_fit[]` recommends for a flow topic and whether F is even considered.

findings.creator: music-industry
findings.topic: the most corrected number in the field, quoted without territory or year
findings.title: `currency` advice — 'ratios over levels', write it to last — manufactures the unqualified rate in a domain where the numbers are policed
findings.expected: Shelf-life advice that recognises a class of domain where a figure stripped of its anchors is not durable but wrong-by-default, and where the correct advice is the opposite: never state the rate without its territory and its period, and accept the shorter shelf life.
findings.got: Phase 5 :83 prefers 'ratios over levels' and `currency.advice` (:85) 'should usually contain a phrasing trick that extends shelf life'; the reference applies it as 'write the price as a ratio and the script survives months instead of days' (notebook.json:411). Applied here it generates 'about a third of a cent a stream' with no territory and no year — the single most corrected sentence in this beat, and the Creator's first listed pet peeve, produced by the methodic as an optimisation and presented as a favour. Durable-and-unanchored is a correction with a longer fuse.
findings.refuter_note: Tested 'is the advice actually wrong, or just wrong for me?' — it is right for a volatile spot price (its origin) and inverted for a contested administered rate. That is a scope defect in a general instruction, not a domain quirk, and it is repairable by one conditional sentence, so content. Tested 'would a competent researcher ignore it?' — the reference did not; it adopted the ratio phrasing wholesale, which is the demonstration.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether the produced notebook's `currency.advice` recommends dropping the qualifiers, and whether the rendered script quotes a rate without territory or period.

findings.creator: music-industry
findings.topic: conclusions about contractual structure, where a motive claim lands on a party to a private contract
findings.title: `unhinged` is defined as a motive claim, with no naming rule for a party to a private contract and no exposure field anywhere in the notebook schema
findings.expected: A leap tier that constrains WHO a motive claim may be made about, and somewhere in the notebook to record what being wrong costs — so 'the label structured the advance so it would never recoup' cannot be generated as colour.
findings.got: `Leap = near|moderate|far|unhinged` with `unhinged` defined as 'a claim about MOTIVE, which is the least verifiable kind of claim there is' (conclusions.ts:32-33). The safeguard is `falsifiableBy` (:54-55), but it constrains checkability, not naming — and in this domain a motive falsifier is inherently uncheckable ('wrong if the contract was intended fairly'), which is exactly the fig-leaf the rubric's conclusions test names. The reference's own unhinged conclusion has a checkable falsifier (a published coin count, :175-176) and therefore does not exercise the failure. NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md has no exposure, legal-risk or naming field at any level.
findings.refuter_note: Held at `uncertain` deliberately, and `undecided` on content_or_lens, because the strongest refutation is unresolved at L1: conclusions are OFF by default (conclusions.ts:15-16 opt-in asymmetry) and a human gates every one, so an unsafe conclusion may never reach a script. That is a real safeguard and L1 cannot tell whether it holds in practice — L1's charitable reading is exactly the blind spot the skill names. This only becomes confirmed if L2 produces a motive claim about a contract counterparty with an uncheckable falsifier. Partly confirms the brief's hypothesis 3, on different grounds: not a living person, a party to a private contract.
findings.l2_priority: Generate conclusions on the royalty topic and inspect every `unhinged` and `far` entry for a motive claim about a named counterparty, then score whether its falsifier is actually checkable.
